summary.text: 次 means “next,” “in sequence,” and “second in rank.” Qin- and Han-period manuscripts attest ordered and ranked uses; the earliest graph has competing interpretations.

formation.text: The character’s earliest construction is disputed. One analysis reads an oracle-bone form as a military-station sign; others see a person exhaling or a speaking figure with possible saliva marks. Shuowen analyzes 次 as 欠 plus 二, with 二 supplying the sound, but this account does not settle the earlier forms.

components.text: One disputed reading of an oracle-bone form identifies an element as an early form of 師 and interprets it as part of a military-station sign. This analysis concerns that historical form, not securely the present graph.
In the same analysis, two strokes indicate an encampment. They are not identified as the character 二 and are not established as components of present 次.

Shuowen identifies 欠 in 次. Other interpretations describe early forms as a person exhaling or a speaking figure with possible saliva marks; they do not establish 欠 as a pictorial part of the earliest graph.
Shuowen assigns 二 a sound role in 次. A Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction gives 二 and 次 a comparable final sequence, but this comparison does not settle 二’s role.

sound_limitation.text: The reported reconstruction comparison does not independently establish that 二 is the phonetic component in 次.

sound.text: In the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese system, 二 and 次 have a comparable final sequence. This is the sound comparison behind the proposal, but it does not establish 二 as 次’s phonetic component.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze examples are recorded, followed by Qin-slip, seal, clerical, and regular-script forms. One interpretation of an oracle-bone graph combines an element identified as an early form of 師 with two strokes indicating an encampment, making a proposed military-station sign. Other interpretations differ, and the proposed scene remains uncertain.

Some bronze forms are described with marks below 欠 or with short strokes. Whether this reflects regularization, corruption, or a meaningful graphic change is unresolved. Shuowen later analyzes the form as 欠 plus 二 and assigns 二 a sound role; that analysis remains disputed.

uncertainties.text: Interpretations of the earliest graph differ: proposals include a military-station sign, a person exhaling, and a speaking figure with possible saliva marks. The available descriptions do not resolve them.
Shuowen’s analysis of 二 as a sound element is historically important, but the reported reconstruction comparison does not independently confirm that role.

No securely dated semantic path connects a proposed early meaning to “next” or “in sequence.” The lodging and tent examples come from transmitted texts whose witnesses are not dated in the cited accounts.

senses.gloss: in sequence; next or second in rank
senses.text: Qin- and Han-period manuscript citations attest 次 for ordered transmission and successive rank. These uses are established by that period but do not show that they were the graph’s original meaning.
Transmitted texts use 次 for lodging or tents. How these uses relate to ranked and ordered meanings is unresolved.

A Han silk manuscript is reported to use 次 to write 恣. This proposed borrowing reuses 次 for another word because of a sound resemblance; it does not describe a change in 次’s meaning. The cited account gives no pronunciations to demonstrate the match.

A Mawangdui manuscript is reported to use 次 where the transmitted Zhouyi has 濟. This proposed borrowing reuses 次 for another word because of a sound resemblance; it is not a change in 次’s meaning. The cited account gives no pronunciations to demonstrate the match.

limitations.text: The Qin- and Han-period attestations do not establish the first occurrence of ordered or ranked uses, or their derivation from any proposed original sense. No semantic link is asserted where the evidence does not demonstrate one.
次 is reported in place of 恣 and 濟 in separate manuscripts, but the cited material gives no pronunciations to demonstrate or independently assess the proposed sound-based borrowings.

No candidate glyph image is available to select: the researched candidates did not include a character specific image with verified reuse terms. The surviving bronze form record is an artifact linked lead, but its image reuse status was not verified.
